# What a commuting law keeps apart

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`what-a-commuting-law-keeps-apart` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](what-a-commuting-law-keeps-apart.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Where a law commutes with a map moving every configuration, its runs from x and from the image of x are never at one configuration at the same step: to merge what a symmetry tells apart, a law must break it. The diagonal's never resting is the case of a map with itself.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A law commuting with σ has its run from σ x the image of its run from x; where σ moves every configuration the two runs never meet at a step, and a law that merges them does not commute. (`Becoming.Law.Commutes`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.iterate`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.apart`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.breaks`)
2. No such law is constant; a run from what σ fixes stays where σ fixes; rests and returns come with their images. (`Becoming.Law.Commutes.not_drawn_to_one`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.keeps_fixed`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.rest_paired`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.returns_paired`)
3. Under an exchange a run holding a configuration's image k steps on holds every configuration's image k steps on and returns at 2k; the law goes alike across the pairs, as a lumping and as a process. (`Becoming.Law.Commutes.paired_halfway`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.halfway_returns`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.pairs_lumped`, `Becoming.Law.Commutes.pairs_goAlike`)
4. Every map commutes with itself, so a map moving every value never rests along its run (Diagonal.revision_never_rests as a case). (`Becoming.Law.Commutes.self_apart`)
5. A process symmetric under σ carries reach, returning and, under an exchange, junctures; every run has a mirror run never at the same configuration at the same step; a commuting law is a symmetric process. (`Becoming.Branching.Symmetric`, `Becoming.Branching.Symmetric.reach`, `Becoming.Branching.Symmetric.returns`, `Becoming.Branching.Symmetric.juncture`, `Becoming.Branching.mirror`, `Becoming.Branching.mirror_apart`, `Becoming.Branching.law_symmetric`)
6. In the Changes the complement moves every hexagram and waxWane commutes with it: no number of steps brings a hexagram and its complement to one, the six steps to the complement are the pair halfway round the return of twelve, the going alike across pairs is the general law's instance, the waning into 坤 breaks the symmetry, and the change of one line is symmetric under the complement. (`Becoming.Hexagram.complement_moves`, `Becoming.Hexagram.waxWane_apart`, `Becoming.Hexagram.waxWane_halfway`, `Becoming.Hexagram.pairs_goAlike_of_commutes`, `Becoming.Hexagram.wane_breaks`, `Becoming.Hexagram.flip_complement`, `Becoming.Hexagram.changes_symmetric`, `Becoming.Hexagram.changes_mirror_apart`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; commuting and σ moving every configuration (or σ an exchange, or fixing x) are the hypotheses each law names; the laws are stated on runs Law.run and on processes.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Groups of symmetries (the four-group of 錯 and 綜, and 互), symmetries with fixed points beyond keeps_fixed, and which symmetries actual unfoldings keep.
- That keeping or erasing a difference is better; the earlier claim that «一» structurally does not exist.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
